In this specification, we will refer to components created by
compiling a file as \emph{simple components}, while components created by
linking components together will be known as \emph{compound
components}.

The source code of a simple component definition
begins with an optional modifier \KWD{native} followed by
\KWD{component} followed by a
\emph{possibly qualified name} (an identifier or a sequence of
identifiers separated by periods with no intervening whitespace),
followed by a sequence of \emph{import} statements,
and a sequence of \emph{export} statements,
and finally a sequence of declarations,
where all sequences are separated by newlines or semicolons.
A component declaration may end with an optional \KWD{component} and its name again.
It is a static error if the identifier after \KWD{end} is not
the name of the component being declared.


\subsection{Import Statements}
An import statement imports declarations from one or more APIs.
There are two forms of import statements.
The first form imports all top-level and functional method declarations
(i.e., declarations whose reach is the entire API)
from the listed APIs,
and allows the names declared by these declarations
to be used \emph{qualified} by the name of the API
from which it is imported.
%import apiName, anotherApiName
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{import} \VAR{apiName}, \VAR{anotherApiName}\)
\end{Fortress}
This form may also provide an \emph{alias}
for one or more of the APIs.
%import apiName as alias, anotherApiName
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{import} \VAR{apiName} \KWD{as} \VAR{alias}, \VAR{anotherApiName}\)
\end{Fortress}
A name imported from an API with an alias
must be qualified by the alias
rather than the name of the API.
It is a static error for any alias
to be the name of any imported API.
Multiple APIs may be given the same alias,
but it is a static error
if declarations imported from two APIs with the same alias
declare the same name
unless the set of imported declarations with that name
from APIs with that alias
form a valid set of overloaded declarations.

There are two forms of import statements: \emph{explicit import statements} and
\emph{on-demand import statements}.

An explicit import statement specifies a single API and a set of names;
it imports the top-level and functional method declarations in the specified API.
It allows the specified names to be used \emph{unqualified}
in the importing component or API:
% import APIName.{ name (, name)^+ }
\begin{Fortress}
\( \KWD{import}\:\TYP{APIName}.\{\,\VAR{name} (, \VAR{name})^+\,\}\)

1	component microgpt2
2	import List.{...}

4	export Executable
5	
6	(* microgpt2.fss -- iteration 2 of the microgpt notation exploration: the
7	   complete model in the merged "carriers (+) tower" design approved in
8	   explorations/microgpt-iteration2-plan.md (Judgment section; decision
9	   brief in the session record).  Karpathy's microgpt -- scalar reverse-mode
10	   autodiff, char-level tokenizer, 1-layer/2-head transformer (rmsnorm,
11	   multi-head attention with KV history, relu MLP), Adam with bias
12	   correction and linear LR decay, temperature sampling -- with the model
13	   level stated in the notation the ML literature itself uses:
14	
15	     h0      = _We[t] + _Wp[i]
16	     RMSNorm  x / SQRT((x DOT x) / d + epsilon)
17	     attend   softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
18	     FFN      _W2 relu(_W1 x)
19	     loss     - log(p[y])
20	
21	   The design, per the judgment: the autodiff node is named Value
22	   (Karpathy's own class name -- freeing the letter V for the value
23	   matrix); Value joins the 2012 library's numeric tower twice
24	   (MultiplicativeRing gives juxtaposition, binary minus, zero as trait
25	   defaults; StandardMax opens the genuine library BIG MAX to the tape,
26	   so softmax's stabilizing shift is a real big operator with no .data
27	   leak); vectors and matrices are carrier objects on the library's own
28	   Potemkin rank traits (Rank1 excludes Rank2 -- the exclusion that makes
29	   BOTH juxtaposition directions legal under the spec's Meet Rule,
30	   advanced/overloading.tex; library precedent FortressLibrary.fss:2634,
31	   2641); Vec extends AdditiveGroup, so the residual stream rides on
32	   carrier-level inherited algebra; ^T is a real superscripted postfix
33	   operator (spec basic/operators/intro.tex special-cases ^T "to signify
34	   matrix transposition"), making the attention line the literature's own;
35	   carrier = is defined (HasRank's default makes even x = x false --
36	   FortressLibrary.fss:1588); weights are _W-prefixed, the spec's
37	   leading-underscore boldface convention (basic/lexical-structure.tex,
38	   render-identifiers), so they typeset as the bold matrices of the
39	   papers; n-ary summation is the named function sum(...) -- the library
40	   SUM is sealed to Number three independent ways (expressiveness-review
41	   finding 7), and the standing rules prefer the named function over a
42	   custom big glyph anyway; per-head plumbing is three per-head
43	   comprehensions, the literature's "head_1 ... head_h" ellipsis made
44	   precise.  Everything else about the architecture matches the Python
45	   reference: 1 layer, heads structural, rmsnorm without gain, no biases,
46	   plain relu, causality by history, Adam beta1 .85 beta2 .99 lr .01
47	   linear decay, BOS = 26, vocab 27.
48	
49	   The harness (data, tokenizer, optimizer, sampling) is held to the same
50	   notational discipline as the model: each stage is a named definition
51	   stated by its own formula, and the Adam sweep is an unordered for --
52	   the per-parameter updates are independent, so only the step loop is
53	   seq (a genuine recurrence).
54	
55	   Verified: v1's goldenCheck numbers (15 logits, mean loss, 5 gradients)
56	   at 1e-9, then a nano training run.  Run FORTRESS_THREADS=1. *)
57	
58	(* ---------- scalar reverse-mode autodiff: the tape engine ---------- *)
59	
60	(* Value is a multiplicative ring and a StandardMax; saying so buys
61	   juxtaposition (= TIMES), binary minus (= self + (-o)), zero, and the
62	   library's genuine BIG MAX, all as trait defaults (precedents:
63	   explorations/complex_ring.fss for the ring; the tower nucleus for MAX). *)
64	object Value(var data: RR64, children: List[\Value\], grads: List[\RR64\])
65	       extends { MultiplicativeRing[\Value\], StandardMax[\Value\] }
66	  getter one(): Value = konst(1.0)
67	  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
68	  var visited: Boolean := false
69	  opr +(self, o: Value): Value = Value(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
70	  opr +(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data + c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
71	  opr TIMES(self, o: Value): Value =
72	    Value(data o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
73	  opr -(self): Value = Value(-data, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
74	  opr /(self, o: Value): Value =
75	    Value(data / o.data, <| self, o |>,
76	          <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
77	  opr /(self, c: RR64): Value = Value(data / c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c|>)
78	  opr /(self, n: ZZ32): Value = self / (n 1.0)
79	  opr ^ (self, n: RR64): Value = Value(data^n, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
80	  opr MAX(self, o: Value): Value = if data >= o.data then self else o end
81	end
82	
83	konst(d: RR64): Value = Value(d, emptyList[\Value\](), emptyList[\RR64\]())
84	
85	exp(v: Value): Value = Value(exp v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] exp v.data|>)
86	log(v: Value): Value = Value(log v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0/v.data|>)
87	relu(v: Value): Value = if v.data > 0.0
88	                        then Value(v.data, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
89	                        else Value(0.0, <| v |>, <|[\RR64\] 0.0|>) end

91	
92	(* Sigma as the literature writes it: a named function, one n-ary Sum
93	   node; the forward value is the genuine library SUM over the addends'
94	   data (they are Numbers), folded sequentially (FP addition is not
95	   associative; the fold order is the reproducibility contract);
96	   d(sum)/d(addend_j) = 1. *)
97	sum(addends: List[\Value\]): Value =
98	  Value(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)

101	object Topo()
102	  var items: List[\Value\] := emptyList[\Value\]()
103	  build(v: Value): () = do
104	    if NOT v.visited then
105	      v.visited := true

116	  t = Topo()
117	  t.build(root)
118	  root.grad := 1.0
119	  for v <- seq(t.items.reverse) do
120	    for (ch, lg) <- seq(v.children.zip[\RR64\](v.grads)) do
121	      ch.grad := ch.grad + lg v.grad
122	    end
123	  end
124	  for v <- t.items do v.visited := false end
125	end
126	
127	(* ---------- the carriers: library citizens ----------
128	   Vec/Mat wrap List; extending the library's own Rank1/Rank2 makes them
129	   mutually excluding, so BOTH juxtaposition directions are legal
130	   overloads; ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed buy |x|, x[i], zip, and full
131	   generator integration (u <- x, BIG ops over x) from three one-line
132	   members; AdditiveGroup gives Vec inherited binary minus and zero from
133	   + and unary -.  Carrier = is defined because HasRank's default
134	   equality is constant false -- even x = x. *)
135	
136	object Vec(xs: List[\Value\])
137	    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\Value\], DelegatedIndexed[\Value,ZZ32\],
138	              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
139	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
140	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
141	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Value = xs[i]
142	  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\Value\](y) |>)
143	  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
144	  opr =(self, y: Vec): Boolean =
145	    (|xs| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[m <- self.indices] ((xs[m]).data = y[m].data))
146	end
147	
148	object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
149	    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
150	  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
151	  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
152	  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
153	  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
154	  opr =(self, y: Mat): Boolean =
155	    (|rows| = |y|) AND (BIG AND[i <- self.indices] (rows[i] = y[i]))
156	end
157	
158	(* ---------- the notation layer: each operator defined once,
159	              by its index formula ---------- *)
160	
161	(* u DOT w = SUM_m u_m w_m : one n-ary Sum node *)
162	opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): Value = sum(<| u[m] w[m] | m <- u.indices |>)
163	
164	(* (W x)_r = W_r DOT x *)
165	opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| r DOT x | r <- w |>)
166	
167	(* (p M)_c = SUM_j p_j M_j_c -- the OTHER direction, legal because
168	   Rank1 excludes Rank2 *)
169	opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
170	  Vec(<| sum(<| p[j] (m[j])[c] | j <- p.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
171	
172	(* (M^T)_c_j = M_j_c : the spec's superscripted postfix operator,
173	   "typically used to signify matrix transposition" (basic/operators/intro.tex) *)
174	opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
175	  Mat(<| Vec(<| (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)
176	
177	(* scalar broadcasts and pointwise lifts *)
178	opr -(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u - s | u <- x |>)
179	opr /(x: Vec, s: Value): Vec = Vec(<| u / s | u <- x |>)
180	opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| u / c | u <- x |>)
181	relu(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| relu u | u <- x |>)
182	exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| exp u | u <- x |>)
183	concat(heads: List[\Vec\]): Vec = Vec(<| u | h <- heads, u <- h |>)
184	
185	(* ---------- the model, block by block ---------- *)
186	
187	epsilon: RR64 = 0.00001
188	
189	(* RMSNorm(x) = x / SQRT(x.x/d + eps) -- no learnable gain; d is the
190	   dimension of x (|x| is length here, not a norm) *)
191	rmsnorm(x: Vec): Vec = do
192	  d = |x|
193	  x / SQRT((x DOT x) / d + epsilon)
194	end
195	
196	(* softmax(a)_j = e^(a_j - m) / SUM_k e^(a_k - m): the stabilizing shift
197	   m = max a is the library's own BIG MAX (Value extends StandardMax), the
198	   pointwise e^(a - m) uses Value's inherited minus, and
199	   softmax(a) = softmax(a - m) is an identity, so the shift changes no
200	   number the mathematics defines. *)
201	softmax(a: Vec): Vec = do
202	  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
203	  e = exp(a - m)
204	  e / sum(e)
205	end
206	
207	(* L = -log softmax(logits)_y *)
208	nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): Value = do
209	  p = softmax(logits)
210	  - log(p[y])
211	end
212	
213	(* one layer, nHead heads; n_layer = 1 as in Karpathy's default.  kh/vh
214	   are the per-head histories of key/value vectors for positions 0..i-1;
215	   forward returns the logits together with the histories extended by
216	   position i -- the KV cache is visible as data, and causality is the
217	   data too: K and V never contain a future position, so no mask. *)
218	object Model(nHead: ZZ32, d_k: ZZ32, _We: Mat, _Wp: Mat, _Wlm: Mat,
219	             _Wq: List[\Mat\], _Wk: List[\Mat\], _Wv: List[\Mat\],
220	             _Wo: Mat, _W1: Mat, _W2: Mat)
221	
222	  (* one head at one step, over its whole history: score, weights, blend
223	     in the literature's own line.  K stacks the head's key vectors as
224	     rows, so (q K^T)_j = q DOT k_j. *)
225	  attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
226	
227	  (* FFN(x) = W_2 relu(W_1 x) *)
228	  ffn(x: Vec): Vec = _W2 relu(_W1 x)
229	
230	  forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
231	      : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
232	    h0 = _We[t] + _Wp[i]
233	    x1 = rmsnorm(h0)
234	    x2 = rmsnorm(x1)
235	    K = <| (kh[h]).addRight(_Wk[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
236	    V = <| (vh[h]).addRight(_Wv[h] x2) | h <- 0#nHead |>
237	    heads = <| attend(_Wq[h] x2, K[h], V[h]) | h <- 0#nHead |>
238	    x3 = _Wo concat(heads) + x1
239	    x4 = rmsnorm(x3)
240	    x5 = ffn(x4) + x3
241	    (_Wlm x5, K, V)
242	  end
243	
244	  (* every weight leaf in one flat list, the optimizer's view of the
245	     model (Karpathy's [p for mat in state_dict.values() for row in mat
246	     for p in row]); Mats and Vecs are generators, so the nested clauses
247	     walk them with no unwrapping *)
248	  params(): List[\Value\] =
249	    (<| p | m <- <| _We, _Wp, _Wlm, _Wo, _W1, _W2 |>, row <- m, p <- row |>
250	     || <| p | hm <- <|[\List[\Mat\]\] _Wq, _Wk, _Wv |>, m <- hm, row <- m, p <- row |>)
251	end
252	
253	emptyHist(nh: ZZ32): List[\Mat\] = <| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>
254	
255	(* ---------- weights ---------- *)
256	
257	wStd: RR64 = 0.08
258	
259	(* Box-Muller; random() is the library native.  wStd is a constant rather
260	   than Karpathy's default argument (matrix(nout, nin, std=0.08)) because
261	   keyword parameters with default expressions -- sanctioned by the spec,
262	   basic/functions.tex:155 -- parse but are unimplemented in the walk
263	   interpreter: InterpreterBug "the number of parameters (2) does not match
264	   with the number of arguments (1)".  Implementation gap, recorded. *)
265	gauss(): RR64 = do
266	  var u1: RR64 := random(1.0)
267	  if u1 < 0.000000000001 then u1 := 0.000000000001 end
268	  u2 = random(1.0)
269	  wStd (SQRT (-2.0 (log u1))) (cos (2.0 3.141592653589793 u2))
270	end
271	
272	gaussMat(rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Mat =
273	  Mat(<| Vec(<| konst(gauss()) | j <- 0#cols |>) | i <- 0#rows |>)
274	gaussHeads(nh: ZZ32, hs: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\Mat\] =
275	  <| gaussMat(hs, cols) | h <- 0#nh |>
276	
277	(* ---------- the harness: data, tokenizer, sampling ---------- *)
278	
279	(* the first k lines of the file.  File.fsi's lines() is a whole-file
280	   generator and lines(n) bounds only the read-ahead chunk, not the
281	   count, so a bounded read is a loop, not a comprehension: the
282	   comprehension form works but overflows the launcher's default 32 MB
283	   stack on names.txt's 32033 lines (recorded in the diet report). *)
284	readDocs(path: String, k: ZZ32): List[\String\] = do
285	  fr = FileReadStream(path)
286	  var docs: List[\String\] := emptyList[\String\]()
287	  while (NOT fr.eof) AND (|docs| < k) do docs := docs.addRight(fr.readLine()) end
288	  fr.close(); docs
289	end
290	
291	(* tokens = BOS doc BOS, a..z mapped to 0..25 -- Karpathy's
292	   [BOS] + [ids] + [BOS], and String is a Char generator so the middle
293	   is one comprehension *)
294	tokenize(doc: String, bos: ZZ32): List[\ZZ32\] =
295	  <|[\ZZ32\] bos|> || <| c.codePoint() - 97 | c <- doc |> || <|[\ZZ32\] bos|>
296	
297	(* sample j with probability p_j: the inverse-CDF rule stated as a count
298	   -- j is the number of prefix sums that fall short of a uniform draw
299	   (the MIN is the floating-point guard, exactly v1's fallback) *)
300	sample(p: Vec): ZZ32 = do
301	  r = random(1.0)
302	  short = <| j | j <- p.indices, (SUM[i <- seq(0#(j + 1))] (p[i]).data) < r |>
303	  |short| MIN (|p| - 1)
304	end
305	
306	(* ---------- golden check: exact model math vs. the Python reference ---------- *)
307	
308	(* deterministic weights for the golden check (no RNG; the same formula
309	   lives in the Python reference generator).  goldRows(mi, r0, rows, cols)
310	   is the row block r0 .. r0+rows-1 of v1's flat matrix mi, so a head's
311	   slice carries exactly v1's values (the flat-row-index mapping). *)
312	initW(i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 = (((31 i + 17 j) REM 97) - 48) / 100.0
313	
314	goldRows(mi: ZZ32, r0: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Mat =
315	  Mat(<| Vec(<| konst(initW(100 mi + r0 + i, j)) | j <- 0#cols |>) | i <- 0#rows |>)
316	
317	goldMat(mi: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Mat = goldRows(mi, 0, rows, cols)
318	
319	goldHeads(mi: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, hs: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\Mat\] =
320	  <| goldRows(mi, h hs, hs, cols) | h <- 0#nh |>
321	
322	goldenCheck(): () = do
323	  nH: ZZ32 = 2
324	  hs: ZZ32 = 2
325	  g = Model(nH, hs,
326	            goldMat(0, 5, 4), goldMat(1, 4, 4), goldMat(2, 5, 4),
327	            goldHeads(3, nH, hs, 4), goldHeads(4, nH, hs, 4), goldHeads(5, nH, hs, 4),
328	            goldMat(6, 4, 4), goldMat(7, 16, 4), goldMat(8, 4, 16))
329	  tol = 10.0^(-9)
330	  tokens = <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 0, 1, 4|>
331	  gold0 = <|[\RR64\] 1.1786640480869652, 0.08369680205708685, -1.2116330341802932, 1.161464590811486, 0.06649734478160751|>
332	  gold1 = <|[\RR64\] -0.5153754312822434, 0.7583368418857922, -0.6709093810270941, -0.44385589510170814, 0.8298563780663275|>
333	  gold2 = <|[\RR64\] -0.7803193651360372, 0.2648497272535788, 0.9794442126538028, -0.861494046699949, 0.18367504568966714|>
334	  golds = <|[\List[\RR64\]\] gold0, gold1, gold2|>
335	  var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(nH), emptyHist(nH))
336	  var losses: List[\Value\] := emptyList[\Value\]()
337	  for pos <- seq(0#3) do
338	    (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(tokens[pos], pos, kh, vh)
339	    kh := kh2
340	    vh := vh2
341	    gold = golds[pos]
342	    for i <- seq(0#5) do
343	      assert(|(logits[i]).data - gold[i]| < tol, "golden logits pos " pos " idx " i)
344	    end
345	    losses := losses.addRight(nll(logits, tokens[pos + 1]))
346	  end
347	  loss = sum(losses) / 3.0
348	  assert(|loss.data - 1.228662661701597| < tol, "golden loss")
349	  backward(loss)
350	  gwte = g._We; gwpe = g._Wp; glm = g._Wlm; gwq = g._Wq; gfc2 = g._W2
351	  assert(|((gwte[4])[0]).grad - (-0.21705452841851058)| < tol, "grad wte[4][0]")
352	  assert(|((gwpe[0])[1]).grad - 0.06350371373725669| < tol, "grad wpe[0][1]")
353	  assert(|((glm[2])[3]).grad - 0.028373522248445866| < tol, "grad lm_head[2][3]")
354	  assert(|(((gwq[0])[0])[0]).grad - (-0.001587106636149662)| < tol, "grad attn_wq[0][0]")
355	  assert(|((gfc2[1])[2]).grad - 0.0101351876799767| < tol, "grad mlp_fc2[1][2]")
356	  println("golden transformer forward/backward vs Python reference: PASS")
357	end
358	
359	(* ---------- training ---------- *)
360	
361	run() = do
362	  goldenCheck()
363	
364	  (* config: BOS = 26, vocab a-z + BOS (names.txt is strictly a-z) *)
365	  vocab: ZZ32 = 27; bos: ZZ32 = 26; maxDocs: ZZ32 = 2000
366	  nEmbd: ZZ32 = 8; nHead: ZZ32 = 2; hs: ZZ32 = nEmbd DIV nHead
367	  blockSize: ZZ32 = 8; numSteps: ZZ32 = 30; temp: RR64 = 0.5
368	
369	  docs = readDocs("explorations/names.txt", maxDocs)
370	  println("num docs: " |docs| "  vocab: " vocab)
371	
372	  g = Model(nHead, hs, gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd), gaussMat(blockSize, nEmbd),
373	            gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd), gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd),
374	            gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd), gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd),
375	            gaussMat(nEmbd, nEmbd), gaussMat(4 nEmbd, nEmbd),
376	            gaussMat(nEmbd, 4 nEmbd))
377	  params = g.params(); nP: ZZ32 = |params|
378	  println("num params: " nP)
379	
380	  (* Adam: m_t = b1 m_{t-1} + (1-b1) g_t;  v_t = b2 v_{t-1} + (1-b2) g_t^2;
381	     mHat = m_t/(1-b1^t);  vHat = v_t/(1-b2^t);  w -= lr_t mHat/(SQRT vHat + eps).
382	     Index-form RR64 on purpose: the literature's Adam IS elementwise
383	     index arithmetic -- and elementwise means independent, so the sweep
384	     over i is an unordered for; only the step loop below is seq. *)
385	  lr0 = 0.01; beta1 = 0.85; beta2 = 0.99; epsA = 0.00000001
386	  mBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)
387	  vBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)
388	
389	  t0 = nanoTime()
390	  for step <- seq(0#numSteps) do
391	    toks = tokenize(docs[step REM |docs|], bos)
392	    n = blockSize MIN (|toks| - 1)
393	    var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(nHead), emptyHist(nHead))
394	    var losses: List[\Value\] := emptyList[\Value\]()
395	    for pos <- seq(0#n) do
396	      (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(toks[pos], pos, kh, vh)
397	      kh := kh2; vh := vh2
398	      losses := losses.addRight(nll(logits, toks[pos + 1]))
399	    end
400	    loss = sum(losses) / (n 1.0)
401	    backward(loss)
402	    lrT = lr0 (1.0 - (step 1.0) / (numSteps 1.0))
403	    st = (step 1.0) + 1.0
404	    for i <- 0#nP do
405	      p = params[i]
406	      mBuf[i] := beta1 mBuf[i] + (1.0 - beta1) (p.grad)
407	      vBuf[i] := beta2 vBuf[i] + (1.0 - beta2) (p.grad)^2.0
408	      mHat = mBuf[i] / (1.0 - beta1^st)
409	      vHat = vBuf[i] / (1.0 - beta2^st)
410	      p.data := p.data - (lrT mHat) / ((vHat^0.5) + epsA)
411	      p.grad := 0.0
412	    end
413	    el = (((nanoTime() - t0) + 500000) DIV 1000000)
414	    println("step " (step + 1) " / " numSteps "  loss " loss.data "  elapsed " el " ms")
415	  end
416	  println("s/step: " (((nanoTime() - t0) 1.0) / (numSteps 1000000000.0)))
417	
418	  (* inference: temperature sampling.  A sample stops at the first BOS,
419	     and tid = bos is exactly that condition once past position 0. *)
420	  println("--- inference ---")
421	  for s <- seq(1#10) do
422	    var (kh, vh): (List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) := (emptyHist(nHead), emptyHist(nHead))
423	    var (tid, out): (ZZ32, String) := (bos, "")
424	    for pos <- seq(0#blockSize) do
425	      if pos = 0 OR tid =/= bos then
426	        (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(tid, pos, kh, vh)
427	        kh := kh2; vh := vh2
428	        tid := sample(softmax(logits / temp))
429	        if tid =/= bos then out := out || char(tid + 97) end
430	      end
431	    end
432	    println("sample " s ": " out)
433	  end
434	end
435	end

(* Q3 probe: since `type` aliases do not exist (p1/p2/p3/p7), the only working
   way to name a space in microgpt2's design is ANOTHER CARRIER OBJECT.  This
   probe asks the decisive structural question: does adding a third Rank1
   carrier (ProbDist) break the flagship's excludes-based overload structure?

   microgpt2.fss declares (lines 165, 169):
       opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec
       opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec
   legal because Rank1 excludes Rank2 (FortressLibrary.fss:1599).
   If softmax returns ProbDist rather than Vec, then microgpt2.fss:225
       attend(q,K,V) = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V
   becomes a ProbDist x Mat juxtaposition and needs its own overload, which
   must coexist with the Vec x Mat one.  Two distinct object types under the
   same rank trait: is that a legal overloading?

   Element type is RR64 here (no autodiff tape) -- overload resolution among
   carriers does not depend on the element type; the shapes are microgpt2's. *)
component p14_named_spaces
import List.{...}
export Executable

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\],
              AdditiveGroup[\Vec\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
  opr +(self, y: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| u + w | (u, w) <- self.zip[\RR64\](y) |>)
  opr -(self): Vec = Vec(<| -u | u <- xs |>)
end

(* a named space with the SAME representation and a DIFFERENT name:
   the paper's  p in Delta^{n-1}  rather than  p in RR^n  *)
object ProbDist(xs: List[\RR64\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "ProbDist" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
end

opr DOT(u: Vec, w: Vec): RR64 = SUM[m <- u.indices] (u[m] w[m])
opr juxtaposition(w: Mat, x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| r DOT x | r <- w |>)
opr juxtaposition(p: Vec, m: Mat): Vec =
  Vec(<| SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

(* THE NEW OVERLOAD the named space forces: ProbDist x Mat *)
opr juxtaposition(p: ProbDist, m: Mat): Vec =
  Vec(<| SUM[j <- p.indices] (p[j] (m[j])[c]) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr (m: Mat)^T : Mat =
  Mat(<| Vec(<| (m[j])[c] | j <- m.indices |>) | c <- (m[0]).indices |>)

opr /(x: Vec, c: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| u / c | u <- x |>)
opr -(x: Vec, s: RR64): Vec = Vec(<| u - s | u <- x |>)
exp(x: Vec): Vec = Vec(<| exp u | u <- x |>)

(* the signature now states the paper's own membership:
     softmax : RR^n -> Delta^{n-1}                                        *)
softmax(a: Vec): ProbDist = do
  m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u
  e = exp(a - m)
  s = SUM[u <- e] u
  ProbDist(<| u / s | u <- e |>)
end

(* microgpt2.fss:225 verbatim in shape, now typed with named spaces *)
attend(q: Vec, K: Mat, V: Mat, d_k: ZZ32): Vec = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V

run() = do
  q  = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>)
  K  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 0.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.0, 1.0|>) |>)
  V  = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 3.0, 4.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 5.0, 6.0|>) |>)
  println("softmax(q K^T/SQRT 2) = " softmax(q K^T / SQRT 2))
  println("attend = " attend(q, K, V, 2))
end

end

(* Q3 probe: the SCALAR named space -- Token / TokenId / Position, all of which
   are ZZ32 in microgpt2.fss (t, i, y, nHead, d_k, blockSize, vocab).
   With no `type` alias, the only route is again a carrier object.  This probe
   measures what that costs for a scalar: every use site that was arithmetic or
   subscripting needs an operator declaration.
   Compare microgpt2.fss:230-232
       forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, ...) = do h0 = _We[t] + _Wp[i] ... *)
component p15_scalar_named
import List.{...}
export Executable

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  (* COST 1: a second subscript overload, one per scalar named space *)
  opr [t: TokenId]: Vec = rows[t.v]
  opr [i: Position]: Vec = rows[i.p]
end

object TokenId(v: ZZ32)
  getter asString(): String = "t" v
end

object Position(p: ZZ32)
  getter asString(): String = "i" p
end

(* the signature now states the paper's own membership:
     t in {0..V-1},  i in {0..T-1}                                       *)
embed(_We: Mat, _Wp: Mat, t: TokenId, i: Position): Vec =
  Vec(<|[\RR64\] u + w | (u, w) <- (_We[t]).zip[\RR64\](_Wp[i]) |>)

run() = do
  _We = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 2.0|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 3.0, 4.0|>) |>)
  _Wp = Mat(<| Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.1, 0.2|>), Vec(<|[\RR64\] 0.3, 0.4|>) |>)
  println("h0 = " embed(_We, _Wp, TokenId(1), Position(0)))
  (* COST 2: the tokenizer, the sampler and every loop bound now sit on the
     wrong side of the wrapper -- .v / .p unwrapping at each boundary *)
  toks = <| TokenId(c) | c <- <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 0, 1|> |>
  println("token ids = " <|[\ZZ32\] (tk.v) | tk <- toks |>)
end

end

(* Q3 probe: the one place in microgpt2.fss where the SAME spelled type means
   two different things.  List[\Mat\] is BOTH
     - the per-head weight bundle   _Wq, _Wk, _Wv : List[\Mat\]   (line 219)
     - the per-head KV history      kh, vh        : List[\Mat\]   (line 230)
   and forward's return type is the opaque (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]).
   With no `type` alias, a carrier object is again the route -- and here it is
   cheap, because a KV cache is only ever indexed by head and extended at the
   right, exactly the two operations a carrier declares in two lines. *)
component p16_kvcache
import List.{...}
export Executable

object Vec(xs: List[\RR64\])
    extends { Rank1, ZeroIndexed[\RR64\], DelegatedIndexed[\RR64,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |xs|
  getter asString(): String = "Vec" xs
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |xs|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: RR64 = xs[i]
end

object Mat(rows: List[\Vec\])
    extends { Rank2, ZeroIndexed[\Vec\], DelegatedIndexed[\Vec,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |rows|
  getter asString(): String = "Mat" rows
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |rows|
  opr [i: ZZ32]: Vec = rows[i]
  addRight(k: Vec): Mat = Mat(rows.addRight(k))
end

(* the named space: one cache, one Mat of history per head *)
object KVCache(heads: List[\Mat\])
    extends { ZeroIndexed[\Mat\], DelegatedIndexed[\Mat,ZZ32\] }
  getter indices(): Generator[\ZZ32\] = 0 # |heads|
  getter asString(): String = "KVCache" heads
  opr |self| : ZZ32 = |heads|
  opr [h: ZZ32]: Mat = heads[h]
  extend(ks: List[\Vec\]): KVCache =
    KVCache(<| (heads[h]).addRight(ks[h]) | h <- self.indices |>)
end

emptyCache(nh: ZZ32): KVCache = KVCache(<| Mat(emptyList[\Vec\]()) | h <- 0#nh |>)

(* before:  forward(...) : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\])
   after :  forward(...) : (Vec, KVCache, KVCache)                        *)
step(nHead: ZZ32, x: Vec, kh: KVCache, vh: KVCache): (Vec, KVCache, KVCache) = do
  K = kh.extend(<| x | h <- 0#nHead |>)
  V = vh.extend(<| x | h <- 0#nHead |>)
  (x, K, V)
end

run() = do
  x = Vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 2.0|>)
  (y, K, V) = step(2, x, emptyCache(2), emptyCache(2))
  (y2, K2, V2) = step(2, x, K, V)
  println("K after two steps = " K2)
  println("|K2[0]| = " |K2[0]|)
end

end

2) give an undefined semantics; and 3) give some operational semantics.
Jan and Guy were for the option 3).
We decided to continue the discussion of the ``story \#1: Arrays'' after Guy's detailed write up.
Meanwhile Jan may work on a semantics for the option 3) and all may discuss syntax issues via emails.  Other stories will be discussed after story \#1.

\item More powerful type aliases

For floating-point numbers, Fortress supports types {$\mathbb{R}$32} and
{$\mathbb{R}$64}
to be 32 and 64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point numbers respectively,
and defines two functions on types:
\EXP{\TYP{Double}\bsTP{F}} is a floating-point type twice the size of the
floating-point type \EXP{F}, and \EXP{\TYP{Extended}\bsTP{F}} is a
floating-point
type sufficiently larger than the floating-point type \EXP{F} to
perform summations of ``reasonable'' size.\footnote{
This formulation of floating-point types follows a proposal under
consideration by the IEEE 754 committee.}

% type Double[\F extends FloatNumber[\e, s, ...\]\] where { nat e, nat s, ... }
%    = FloatNumber[\e+3, 2 s - 6, ... \]
\begin{Fortress}
{\tt~}\pushtabs\=\+\( \KWD{type}\:\TYP{Double}\llbracket{}F \KWD{extends}\:\TYP{FloatNumber}\llbracket{}e, s, \ldots\rrbracket\rrbracket \KWD{where} \{\,\KWD{nat}\:e, \KWD{nat}\:s, \ldots\,\}\)\\
{\tt~~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(    = \TYP{FloatNumber}\llbracket{}e+3, 2 s - 6, \ldots\,\rrbracket\)\-\-\\\poptabs\poptabs
\end{Fortress}

\item \ignore

We're considering supporting \ignore\ (pronounced ``whatever'') not only for
variables but also for type variables.
